title: Man. Post. Cap. IV: GAR — duplex justitia viae / patriae
pass_a_gloss: GAR. This again we deny. Because the justice and sanctity of Adam can be constituted as twofold. One natural, the other supernatural: one of the way, the other of the homeland; one of created man, the other of glorified man. The natural justice and of created man which can be called justice of the way was the condition of the promise; but the supernatural, and of glorified man, which we call justice of the homeland, was the thing promised.
pass_b_english: GAR. We deny this again. Adam's justice and sanctity admit a twofold account: natural versus supernatural; of the way versus of the homeland; of created man versus of glorified man.
Natural justice—created man's justice of the way—was only the condition of the promise. Supernatural justice—glorified man's justice of the homeland—was the thing promised.
source_text: GAR. Hoc iterum inficiamur. Quia justitia & sanctitas Adami duplex constitui potest. Altera naturalis, altera supernaturalis: altera viae, altera patriae; altera hominis creati, altera hominis glorificati. Justitia naturalis & hominis creati quae justitia viae dici potest, erat conditio promissionis; sed supernaturalis, & hominis glorificati, quam dicimus justitiam patriae, erat res promissa.
